rows.name: history-0-audio
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer:
A CUDA warp is a group of 32 threads that the GPU schedules together to execute instructions. Each thread has its own registers and data, but threads in a warp generally execute the same instruction on different data—CUDA calls this SIMT, or single instruction, multiple threads.

If threads take different branches, that’s warp divergence: the GPU executes the different paths with only the appropriate lanes active, which can reduce performance. Memory access also matters: when neighboring threads access neighboring, properly aligned addresses, the GPU can combine those accesses into fewer memory transactions.

Modern GPUs support independent thread scheduling, so don’t assume threads stay synchronized just because they share a warp; use __syncwarp() when you need explicit warp-level synchronization.
